introduction: Legal Aid of Arkansas now serves all 75 Arkansas counties. It offers free civil legal services for eligible low-income residents, with assistance ranging from advice to representation depending on case priorities and resources.

who: The organization evaluates household income, assets and the legal matter. Different kinds of cases can have different eligibility limits or exceptions.

Civil problems may qualify, including housing, consumer, family and benefit issues. Criminal charges and traffic tickets generally fall outside its work; ask about a particular issue before assuming every court matter is excluded.
sections.get: The accepted service may be advice, limited document help, referral or legal representation. Financial eligibility does not guarantee a lawyer for the entire case. Current statewide coverage replaces older regional county lists.
sections.docs: Prepare income information, the parties’ names and papers explaining the legal problem. Flag a hearing, eviction or appeal deadline immediately. Keep originals and ask how to supply copies securely.
sections.apply:
1. Use the Apply for Legal Aid link on the current website or call 1-800-952-9243.
  2. Answer the eligibility and case questions, including your location and urgent dates.
  3. Keep intake details and follow instructions for records. For housing discrimination, the site also lists a dedicated fair-housing helpline at 1-870-338-9834.
sections.after: Confirm what help has been accepted and who handles upcoming tasks. Track deadlines while intake is pending. If the organization cannot represent you, ask about brief advice, clinics or referrals.

faqs: Is coverage still limited to the former county list?
No. The current organizational overview says Legal Aid serves all 75 Arkansas counties after its 2026 expansion.
Does every eligible applicant receive full representation?
No. Staff review priorities and resources; assistance can be advice or limited services instead.
Can it help with a denied benefit?
Public-benefit problems are among its listed civil practice areas. Apply so staff can evaluate the issue and deadline.
Where can I ask about housing discrimination?
The site lists the fair-housing helpline at 1-870-338-9834.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
